title: Natural total-complex comparison for an additive functor
statement: Let $C$ and $D$ be preadditive categories [def-weil-preadditive-category], let $F:C\to D$ be additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], and let $B$ be an integer-indexed commuting bicomplex in $C$: objects $B^{p,q}$ with maps $d_1:B^{p,q}\to B^{p+1,q}$, $d_2:B^{p,q}\to B^{p,q+1}$, $d_1^2=d_2^2=0$, $d_1d_2=d_2d_1$. Its diagonal total has terms $\operatorname{Tot}(B)^n=\coprod_{p+q=n}B^{p,q}$ with injections $\iota_{p,q}$ and differential induced on the $(p,q)$ summand by $d_1+(-1)^p d_2$; $FB$ is the bicomplex obtained by applying $F$ to all objects and differentials. Assume that the diagonal coproducts defining $\operatorname{Tot}(B)$ and the diagonal coproducts defining $\operatorname{Tot}(F B)$ exist, and that $F$ preserves every diagonal coproduct of $B$. Let $c_B^n:\operatorname{Tot}(FB)^n\to F(\operatorname{Tot}(B)^n)$ be the canonical comparison, the unique map with $c_B^n\circ\iota_{p,q}=F(\iota_{p,q})$ for all $p+q=n$. Then the maps $c_B^n$ are isomorphisms and form an isomorphism of cochain complexes $c_B:\operatorname{Tot}(F B)\cong F(\operatorname{Tot}(B))$, the differential on the right being $F$ applied termwise to that of $\operatorname{Tot}(B)$. For every bicomplex map $\phi:B\to B'$ such that $B'$ satisfies the same existence and preservation hypotheses, $c_{B'}\circ\operatorname{Tot}(F\phi)=F(\operatorname{Tot}(\phi))\circ c_B$, and equivalently $c_{B'}^{-1}\circ F(\operatorname{Tot}(\phi))=\operatorname{Tot}(F\phi)\circ c_B^{-1}$.
